author: Neville Goddard
rights_note: Delivered in public spoken lecture on 1968-06-07 in the United States; public domain under 1909 US Copyright Act.
quote_original: Then go your way knowing the desire is now yours.
context_before: Now when you pray you must immerse yourself in the feeling of the wish fulfilled, for the word “pray” means, “Motion towards; accession to; at or in the vicinity of.” Point yourself towards the wish fulfilled and accept that invisible state as reality.
context_after: You did it and you will not be surprised when it comes to pass.
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from There Is No Fiction (1968-06-07).

author: Neville Goddard
rights_note: Delivered in public spoken lecture on 1968-06-07 in the United States; public domain under 1909 US Copyright Act.
quote_original: Imagination truly creates out of nothing!
context_before: true, is not the spirit of God upon man? Yes! Because God actually became as you are, that you may be as He is. Accept this literally, for it is true.
context_after: Thoughts call forth a thing that is not seen, as though it were happening. This is accomplished by an imaginal concept touched by feeling.
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from There Is No Fiction (1968-06-07).

author: Neville Goddard
rights_note: Delivered in public spoken lecture on 1968-06-07 in the United States; public domain under 1909 US Copyright Act.
quote_original: Would you like to be known?
context_before: Everything here will collapse, but because this is a fictitious world you can have anything you want.
context_after: To fulfill a great ambition? To be famous in the eyes of others? You can have them all, if you are willing to assume they are already yours. And, in spite of the evidence of your senses and the contradiction of your reason, if you walk and sleep in your assumption it will harden into fact. And after you have experienced them you will depart, leaving them all behind.
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from There Is No Fiction (1968-06-07).

author: Neville Goddard

quote_original: So I maintain there is no fiction!
context_before: Your desire is brought into being by an imaginal act. It is sustained by an imaginal act, and when that imaginal act is withdrawn (or modified) your desire – fulfilled – will collapse and vanish.
context_after: A friend sent me a copy of the June issue of Harper’s Magazine, which tells of a trial of a captain in our Air Force. As a school project this captain
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from There Is No Fiction (1968-06-07).

author: Neville Goddard
rights_note: Delivered in public spoken lecture on 1968-06-07 in the United States; public domain under 1909 US Copyright Act.
quote_original: Can you believe what you are imagining?
context_before: The secret is to imagine to the point of self-persuasion.
context_after: There are not two of you – you and Imagination! You are not reshaping a piece of pottery when you imagine, but yourself! You are moving into your desire. If you persist until you see exactly what you want to see, fix your position with the glue of feeling and remain there – it will be reflected on the screen of space, just as your world is now reflecting the fixed state from which you are viewing it.
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from There Is No Fiction (1968-06-07).

author: Neville Goddard
rights_note: Delivered in public spoken lecture on 1968-06-07 in the United States; public domain under 1909 US Copyright Act.
quote_original: Believe me, there is no fiction!
context_before: you are destined to become a life-giving spirit – to fashion things in your own image, bring them forth, and endow them with the power to create life.
context_after: Every thought you think will come to pass. You may think it is just a thought and will never become real, but it will.
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from There Is No Fiction (1968-06-07).

author: Neville Goddard
rights_note: Delivered in public spoken lecture on 1968-06-07 in the United States; public domain under 1909 US Copyright Act.
quote_original: These are facts memory has recorded.
context_before: This steward falsified the record, the facts of life which memory claimed to be correct. Perhaps memory says you only have ten dollars in the bank, the rent is due, and there are no prospects of more money on its way. Or that your friend is ill or out of a job.
context_after: You can falsify that record by a permissible lie, by seeing a thousand dollars in the bank and the rent as paid. By seeing one who is ill – as well, or one who is unemployed – as gainfully employed.
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from There Is No Fiction (1968-06-07).

author: Neville Goddard
rights_note: Delivered in public spoken lecture on 1968-06-07 in the United States; public domain under 1909 US Copyright Act.
quote_original: This entire chapter supports my theory.
context_before: The stories I have spoken of come from the eleventh chapter of the Book of Mark.
context_after: I urge you to have faith in God! He is not on the outside. He is not even near, because God actually becomes you! You will know you are He, when God’s son, David, calls you Father. I can tell you that from now until the end of time God became you, but only when his son calls you Father, will you know who you really are.
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from There Is No Fiction (1968-06-07).
